Duration.parse/1 was running a regex per component with a trailing (.*) that copied the remainder each time: 16us/value. Replaced with a length scan plus a slice, keeping Integer.parse/Float.parse for the arithmetic so no float rounds differently. 1.63us/value, verified identical over 200,000 generated well-formed and malformed durations against the previous implementation.

TypeDB.CallOptions validates the option keys of every public function that takes them (query/4, transaction/5, Transaction.open/4, query/3, analyze/3, commit/2, rollback/2, close/2), raising ArgumentError that names the bad key, the call, and the accepted set. test/typedb/call_options_test.exs checks both directions plus a mechanical guard that every public function with a keyword() argument has a row in the table; both guards verified by breaking them.

bench/given.exs measures all three strategies; at 2,000 rows given_rows is 101ms against 1541ms for one request carrying 2,000 insert statements and 8830ms for 2,000 requests. Published in the README and on Transaction.query/3.

Integration test holds a :schema transaction for 500ms and asserts a one-shot on the default waits for it while a one-shot :read does not; verified non-vacuous by switching the blocked call to :read and watching it fail. README now states the measured behaviour rather than only naming the lock.

:max_keep_alive_length now defaults to 0, so :httpc never queues a request behind one already in flight. Verified against a live server (blocked 557ms / unblocked 5ms, against 10s timeouts for both before) and by a unit test that runs a slow request beside a fast one through all three adapters, confirmed to fail on the old default. Concurrent throughput improved as well: 437 req/s vs 368 at 64-way.

TypeDB.HTTP.Finch.terminate/1 catches errors as well as exits (OTP 29's proc_lib:stop/3 raises :timeout_value rather than exiting when the remaining timeout lands at or below zero), and Connection.terminate/2 contains anything an adapter's terminate/1 does. Covered by a test adapter that raises, throws, exits and errors; verified by removing the containment and watching three of five fail.

ci.yml gained token_renewal and tls jobs, both starting TypeDB with docker run because a service container cannot take the flags they need. Verified green in CI (run 30745938744) with the token suite taking 27s and the TLS suite reporting '3 passed' per adapter — not skips. Each job now fails if its suite skips itself.

guides/recipes.md covers paging (and why sort is not optional), streaming, bulk load, upsert and why put is not one, counting, batch delete, to_struct, and a boot-time migration. Every recipe was run against a live 3.12.1 before it was written down, and test/integration/recipes_integration_test.exs runs the same queries on every push.

2 MiB request-body limit bisected against 3.12.1 (2047 KiB accepted, 2048 KiB not), documented in the recipes guide with a byte-aware chunk_while that was itself run against a live server, in the errors guide's code table, and on Transaction.query/3. An integration test pins both sides of the boundary. Also recorded that a body far over the limit closes the socket and therefore presents as a retryable :transport failure.

TypeDB.CallOptions now checks option values as well as names, with the same rules TypeDB.Config applies (positive integers, timeouts, booleans), raising ArgumentError that names the option, the value and the call. nil stays 'unset' everywhere. A cross-level test drives both Config and every per-call function through the same table of bad values so the two cannot drift; it caught the first draft rejecting nil, which Config accepts.
